However it does not implement the task semantics: (1) it rewards reaching the exit from u1 regardless of whether the box is being held — `at_exit` from u1 is reachable right after `box_fell` emptied the hands? No, actually after box_fell you go to u2, and from u2, `holding_box & !at_exit` returns to u1 — but note u2 -> u1 requires `holding_box & !at_exit`, so exiting while holding works via u1->u3. Also u2->u1 via `holding_box & !at_exit` allows arbitrarily delayed re-pickup, ignoring the 'very next move' requirement.
